A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EPG research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and reorganized material.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet diffusion and consistency generation results, scaling experiments, and appendix ablations and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds larger-model results, training-time comparisons, loss-component and encoder-update ablations, and feature visualizations.

M1.justification: The two-stage pre-training and fine-tuning procedure, temperature schedule, encoder-decoder components, and auxiliary consistency-model loss are retained. InfoNCE is renamed NT-Xent without changing Equation (7), and the frozen auxiliary encoder is renamed W_phi. XXL/G scale the existing decoder architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K for diffusion and consistency generation, including ImageNet-224 ablations and ImageNet-256/512 benchmarks. The added analyses and class-balanced sampling retain the same data domains, classes, and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RAE, PixNerd, PixelFlow, SiD2, and JiT-H/G comparisons while removing U-ViT-H/2 and CDM. Table 2 adds PixNerd, printed as PixelNerd. The earlier ablation comparators remain in v2 Table 6; its new REPA SiT-B label conflicts with Appendix B.1's SiT-L/16 description, so a REPA backbone replacement is not established.

E3.justification: v2 adds 789M/1391M models, comparisons extending to 1600 epochs, class-balanced sampling, and frozen versus layer-wise encoder-update controls. It revises the ablation sampler description from Euler-Maruyama to deterministic Euler and noise shifting from 256/64 to image_size/64. Appendix weight-decay assignments also change. The CM training count changes from 600K to 700K in the appendix, matching v1's main text; these reporting revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The existing auxiliary-loss and temperature ablations become Table 12a/b. v2 adds contrastive-loss removal and scratch controls in Table 12c, encoder freezing and learning-rate-decay tests in Table 13, encoder-feature comparisons in Figures 5–6, and convergence curves in Figure 7. These substantially extend tests of component roles and training behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for generation results. The across-sample representation-standard-deviation diagnostic is retained unchanged as v1 Figure 4 and v2 Figure 8.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the 2.04-FID XL result and adds XXL/G results, including 1.58 FID with a 1391M model, 1600 epochs, and class-balanced sampling, versus the earlier headline's 583M model and 800 epochs. Table 5 adds DiT's 506-hour timing; Tables 12c/13 add loss-removal and encoder-update results. Reported ImageNet-512 FID 2.35 and one-step CM FID 8.82 remain unchanged. REPA's reported NFE changes from 422 to 434.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly specifies the mathematical time grid in Equation (10), together with explicit input-preconditioning and time-conditioning formulas. This is a limited addition to the formal specification. The SDE/ODE development and losses in Equations (1)–(9) retain their substance, and no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central two-stage, VAE-free generation and high-resolution consistency-model contributions remain. The abstract strengthens the performance and efficiency claim from rivaling latent methods at comparable cost to a 1.58-FID headline and approximately 30% of DiT's training compute. Existing semantic-consistency and resolution-scaling arguments receive greater prominence in the contribution list.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new ablations as showing that contrastive learning prevents harmful initialization and encoder adaptation supplies low-level information. It newly attributes the advantage over JiT to semantic learning and links pixel-only prediction to overfitting. Section 6 adds an explicit limitations discussion attributing the remaining REPA/RAE gap largely to compute rather than a fundamental constraint; these causal interpretations exceed what the comparisons alone isolate.

D1.justification: Appendix B expands implementation disclosure with the time grid, conditioning formulas and constants, separate encoder configurations, XXL/G architecture details, additional hardware/timings, and rRCM's pre-training length. Code-access information is unchanged. Some detail is lost: the main benchmark's CFG scale of 2.5 and REPA's explicit 0.5 alignment coefficient disappear. The newly stated preconditioning formula also conflicts with Table 9.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to JiT, RAE, PixNerd, PixelFlow, SiD2, SimCLR, and rectified flow, while removing DINO, contrastive predictive coding, and the early-stopped REPA work. The established related-work structure and positioning relative to rRCM and USP remain largely intact, with focused new discussion of JiT scalability and the RAE performance gap.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, revises the introduction and contribution list, separates diffusion and consistency fine-tuning explanations, and reorganizes experimental descriptions. Training discussion moves into Appendix B.2, the conclusion becomes a broader Discussion section, and the appendices are reorganized around expanded analyses.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn; v2 adds an architecture diagram, feature visualizations, convergence plots, and timing/configuration/ablation displays. Table 1 distinguishes class-balanced results visually, and Table 2 corrects the swapped latent/pixel groupings. Existing auxiliary-loss and temperature tables are merged, while unchanged sample galleries are redistributed across appendix pages.

improvement.justification: The added DiT timing comparison and loss-component/encoder-update controls strengthen support for the efficiency and representation-learning claims. Updated baselines and corrected Table 2 groupings also improve assessment of competitiveness. These gains are tempered by stronger causal claims that the controls do not establish and mixed reproducibility edits, including omitted guidance strength and conflicting preconditioning formulas. The lower headline FID uses different model, budget, and sampling settings; the net improvement is useful but limited.
